أكثر من 3 مليار مستخدم نشِط شهريًا على منصة الإنتاجية الأكثر شهرةً في العالم. أليس الوقت مناسبًا للحصول على عنوان بريد إلكتروني مخصّص للعمل؟ باستخدام Workspace وGmail، سيصبح من السهل إعداد بريد إلكتروني لنشاطك التجاري ينتهي بـ ‎@yourbusiness. بالإضافة إلى ذلك، ستتوفّر لك إمكانية الوصول إلى حزمة كاملة من أدوات التعاون والإنتاجية لنشاطك التجاري. مزيد من المعلومات تعرَّف على كيفية إنشاء حساب Gmail باستخدام نطاقك الخاص والهوية البصرية للعلامة التجارية أساسيات البريد الإلكتروني للنشاط التجاري كيفية إعداد حساب بريد إلكتروني لنشاطك التجاري الاشتراك في Google Workspace يمكنك تجربته بدون تكلفة في أول 14 يومًا. وبعدها، يمكنك اختيار خطة تلائم احتياجات نشاطك التجاري. البدء ربط نطاقك أو شراء اسم نطاق من السهل ربط نطاق. فعند الاشتراك، يمكنك استخدام Google Workspace للعثور على جهات التسجيل لشراء نطاق أو ربط نطاق حالي. مزيد من المعلومات إنشاء جميع عناوين بريدك الإلكتروني يمكنك إعداد عناوين البريد الإلكتروني للموظفين والعناوين البديلة للبريد الإلكتروني مثل sales@yourcompany. وبذلك تكون جاهزًا لتفعيل Gmail. مزيد من المعلومات مزايا "Gmail للأنشطة التجارية" عنوان بريد إلكتروني في نطاق خاص من خلال Gmail هو الأفضل للنشاط التجاري الحفاظ على أمانك باستخدام إعدادات الأمان المتقدّمة جميع حسابات Gmail للأنشطة التجارية تتوفّر فيها ميزات مثل المصادقة الثنائية والحماية من التصيّد الاحتيالي (يحظر Gmail الهجمات بنسبة %99.9 قبل وقوعها) للمساعدة في الحفاظ على أمان المستخدمين. مزيد من المعلومات يتضمّن مساحة تخزين إضافية للبريد الإلكتروني يمكنك تخزين جميع رسائلك الإلكترونية وملفاتك المخصّصة للعمل، وذلك من خلال مساحة تخزين إضافية في حساب Gmail للنشاط التجاري أكبر من المساحة المخصّصة للحساب الشخصي. مزيد من المعلومات إدارة وصول الموظفين ليتناسب مع نموّ نشاطك التجاري يتميّز Gmail بقابلية التوسّع ليستوعب نموّ نشاطك التجاري من أول موظّف لديك وحتى المئات من الموظّفين. يمكنك إضافة الموظّفين وإدارة وصولهم إلى البريد الإلكتروني بسهولة على الأجهزة. مزيد من المعلومات تخصيص البريد الإلكتروني يمكنك تخصيص حسابك على Gmail لنشاطك التجاري باستخدام شعارك الخاص وعلامتك التجارية، للتعبير عن هوية نشاطك التجاري. أنشِئ تنسيقات الرسائل المخصّصة بعلامتك التجارية وخصِّص الرسائل باستخدام ميزة دمج البريد. مزيد من المعلومات الأسئلة الشائعة حول البريد الإلكتروني للنشاط التجاري اطّلِع على مزيد من المعلومات حول إنشاء عنوان بريد إلكتروني لنشاطك التجاري واستخدامه. توسيع الكل تتطلب خطط Google Workspace اشتراكًا للوصول إلى الميزات المدفوعة مثل إصدار Gmail بلا إعلانات في نطاق شركة مخصّص، والدعم على مدار 24 ساعة طوال أيام الأسبوع، ومساحة التخزين المحسَّنة في Gmail و Google Drive ، والمزيد . يستخدم Gmail معايير أمان رائدة في المجال لحماية بيانات النشاط التجاري وحظر أكثر من %99.9 من الرسائل غير المرغوب فيها والتصيّد الاحتيالي والبرامج الضارة حتى لا تصل إلى المستخدمين. يستخدم Gmail أيضًا بروتوكول أمان طبقة النقل (TLS) لتشفير الرسائل الإلكترونية أثناء النقل. مزيد من المعلومات نعم، يمكنك استخدام حساب شخصي على Gmail لنشاطك التجاري. وتتوفّر لك مزايا عديدة من خلال استخدام عنوان بريد إلكتروني مخصّص للنشاط التجاري. مزيد من المعلومات بالنسبة إلى الأنشطة التجارية الفردية و"أصحاب المبادرات الفردية" الذين لا يحتاجون إلى نطاق خاص، يمكن تجربة Google Workspace Individual . إذا كنت تحتاج فقط إلى ربط حساب بريد إلكتروني حالي لنشاط تجاري، يمكنك الاشتراك في خطة Workspace التي تلائم نشاطك التجاري. تقدّم خطة اشتراك Google Workspace Individual للأنشطة التجارية الفردية و"أصحاب المبادرات الفردية" ميزات مدفوعة لا تتطلب نطاق عنوان بريد إلكتروني في نطاق خاص. مزيد من المعلومات خصّص البريد الإلكتروني أنشِئ عنوان بريد إلكتروني في نطاق خاص من خلال Gmail اليوم، واعرض المظهر الاحترافي لنشاطك التجاري. Home Discover Play Nearby Favorites The Lab Sign in Loading… Art's Greatest Hidden Meanings Discover the clandestine messages you might have missed in some of the world's greatest artworks Great art is able to convey so much more than just colour and form. It can communicate emotions and ideas
column2: tell stories and even challenge and confuse. Not all of this is immediately evident and it can take time and effort to work out the true meaning of any work. For the most part
column3: the artist wants the viewer to understand the context and meaning of any painting. But that’s not always the case. Sometimes artists include hidden messages in their work
column4: hiding them away so that only a select few people can understand their true significance. Below we look at five paintings and discover the hidden messages not everybody was supposed to see. Café Terrace at Night Vincent Van Gogh
column5: 1888 Painted in 1888
column6: Van Gogh’s classic is one of his most recognizable works. The scene depicts a seemingly ordinary café on a cobbled street. A waiter stands to take an order while patrons sit around leisurely. However
column7: scholars have begun to believe the painting features an homage to Leonardo da Vinci. The twelve figures at the back sit beneath what looks like a cross. It also transpires Van Gogh declared a ‘tremendous need for religion’ in a letter to his brother around this time. The 12 sit along one side of their tables
column8: like Leonardo's disciples
column9: and a shadowy figure departs the scene like Judas. The Last Supper Leonardo da Vinci
column10: 1490s Of course
column11: The Last Supper itself is said to contain hidden messages. As one of the most famous paintings in history
column12: and a deeply important religious work
column13: it's not surprising that people have often looked hard for deeper meanings. In 2007
column14: an Italian musician claimed to have found a selection of musical notes in the painting
column15: hidden in bread rolls and other table features. When played they create a 40-second composition. It’s not impossible
column16: given that Leonardo was a fine musician himself. El Autobus Frida Kahlo
column17: 1929 Not all hidden meanings are meant to be publicly discovered. This is especially true of Kahlo’s El Autobus . What appears to be a simple depiction of Mexican society laid out on a wooden bench at a bus stop may have a more personal tone. Four years before she painted it
column18: Kahlo had been involved in a bus accident that left a permanent scar. The woman to the right of the picture appears to be Kahlo and the man in the blue overalls apparently bears a striking resemblance to the man who pulled an iron bar from her stomach after the accident. An Accident L.S. Lowry
column19: 1926 L.S Lowry’s pictures are renowned for depicting working class life in the north west during the early to mid 20th century. His matchstick figures have entered the popular consciousness
column20: even inspiring a song. However
column21: his pictures are more than just happy matchstick people going about their day. Many contain small scenes of hardship and despair. This is particularly true of 1926’s An Accident which may feature a scene inspired by a local tragedy – giving his works a much deeper social meaning. The Sistine Chapel Michelangelo
column22: 1477-1480 One of the great figures of the Renaissance
column23: Michelangelo took years to create his masterpiece on the Sistine Chapel ceiling. However
column24: there may be more on display than simply incredible beauty. Art historians believe his work contains several hidden anatomical sketches
column25: including an image of the human brain
column26: disguised in the creation scene. This is believed to be a criticism of the Church’s attitudes to the science and discovery that was happening all around. Now you know about some of art's great hidden meanings. You can find out more about da Vinci and how he painted here . column10: he grew up in a liberal family exposed to manga and animation. As a boy he also had a love for insects reminiscent of Fabre

column13: later incorporated the ideogram for "insect" into his pen name. Having developed an intense understanding of the preciousness of life from his wartime experience
column14: Tezuka Osamu aimed to become a physician and later earned his license
column15: but ultimately chose the profession he loved best: manga artist and animated film writer. Tezuka Osamu's manga and animated films had a tremendous impact on the shaping of the psychology of Japan's postwar youth. His work changed the concept of the Japanese cartoon
column16: transforming it into an irresistible art form and incorporating a variety of new styles in creating the "story cartoon." Changing the face of literature and movies
column17: his work also influenced a range of other genres. His impact on animated film was equal to that which he had on the manga world. The lovable characters appearing in works such as Japan's first animated TV series "ASTRO BOY
column18: the color animated TV series Jungle Emperor Leo"
column19: and the two-hour animated special "Bander Book
column20:
captured the hearts of the Japanese through the medium of television, propelling the animated film to tremendous popularity in Japanese general society. Tezuka Osamu's work was exported to the U.S., Europe, and other Asian countries, becoming the stuff of dreams for children around the world. He also ventured into the world of full-length adult animation, exploring all possibilities of the field of animation. In addition to his record of achievement in TV and commercial animation, he also received international acclaim for his work in experimental animation in his later years. His enduring theme that of the preciousness of life, formed the crux of all of Tezuka Osamu's works. Tezuka Osamu, creator of a great cultural asset and gifted with an unbeatable pioneering spirit combined with an enduring passion for his work and a consistent view to the future, lived out his entire life tirelessly pursuing his efforts, passing away at the age of 60 on February 8th, 1989. Home Discover Play Nearby Favorites The Lab Sign in Loading… The birth of the Eiffel tower A realized utopia Eiffel Tower You are at the top of the Eiffel Tower, overlooking Paris at a height of almost 300 m / 1000 feet. At the opening of the Tower in 1889, this very place was different from what you are seeing. Le Campanile et le Phare de la tour Eiffel - Les merveilles de l'Exposition 1889 by © Collection tour Eiffel Eiffel Tower It was used, in particular, as a laboratory to carry out scientific experiments and measurements. Many instruments were installed here such as barometers, anemometers, lightning conductors. In fact, Gustave Eiffel arranged an office for himself at the very top of the Tower for astronomical and physiological observations. He even installed a weather station. It was these scientific experiments carried at the Tower which saved it from being destroyed by popular demand. Did you know the Tower should have been pulled down just 20 years after it was erected for the 1889 Exposition Universelle! From then on until the end of the Monarchy in 1918
column12: almost all the Prussian kings left their stamp on the complex in the shape of alterations

column14: focusing in particular on the role given to contemporary art in the reconstruction. Numerous hitherto unpublished photographs and newly discovered archival material present a picture of the palace from a largely unfamiliar perspective. column2: By Google Arts & Culture Stadium, Olympia, Greece It all began here. In 776 BCE, the first Olympic Games were held in this 45,000 seat stadium, found to the east of the sanctuary of Zeus. The event was a religious festival, and the only sport was the stade , a straight-line sprint of just over 192 metres. Panathenaic Stadium, Athens, Greece The last Olympic Games of the ancient world were held in 393CE. When the first modern games were held in 1896, they were hosted at the Panathenaic Stadium in Athens. The stadium is itself ancient, built in 144CE and refurbished for the 1896 games. Olympic Stadium, Stockholm, Sweden Designed by architect Torben Grut, the Stockholm Olympic Stadium was opened in 1912. During the 1912 Games, it hosted the athletics, tug of war, and wrestling events, and some of the equestrian, football, and gymnastics events. Los Angeles Memorial Coliseum, Los Angeles, USA Conceived as a hallmark of civic pride, the Los Angeles Memorial Coliseum was commissioned in 1921 as a monument to L.A. veterans of the First World War. It has twice hosted the Summer Games, in 1932 and 1984, and is due to host the 2028 Summer Games. Olympiastadion, Berlin, Germany The Berlin Olympiastadion was built specially for the 1936 games, infamous for being hosted by the Nazi government of Germany and being the last games held prior to the Second World War. The games also saw the triumph of Jesse Owens, winner of four gold medals. Olympiastadion, Helsinki, Finland Helsinki had been due to host the 1940 Games, but this was postponed to 1952. The 1952 Games were notable for being the first to feature the USSR, and for the number of world records that were made - many remained unbeaten until 2008. Estadio Olímpico Universitario, Mexico City, Mexico During the 200m medal ceremony on October 16, 1968, two African-American athletes, Tommie Smith and John Carlos, each raised a black-gloved fist during the playing of the US national anthem - an enduring symbol of Black Power and solidarity. Olympic Stadium, Montreal, Canada One of the most iconic stadia of the games. The Montreal Olympic stadium was built as the main venue for the 1976 Summer Olympics. Nicknamed 'The Big O' for its name and ring-shaped roof, it's also known as 'The Big Owe' for the huge cost of its construction. Stadium Australia, Sydney, Australia Sydney was host to the first games of the third Millennium, when it held the Summer Games in 2000. Since then, it's been renovated and come to host Australia's national games: cricket and Australian rules football. Spyros Louis" Olympic Stadium

column4: Gentileschi was the first woman to become a member of the Accademia di Arte del Disegno in Florence and she had an international clientele. Many of Gentileschi's paintings feature women from myths
column5: allegories
column6: and the Bible
column7: including victims
column8: suicides
column9: and warriors. Some of her best known subjects are Susanna and the Elders
column10: Judith Slaying Holofernes
column11: and Judith and Her Maidservant. Gentileschi was known for being able to depict the female figure with great naturalism and for her skill in handling colour to express dimension and drama. column3: 1944 Edvard Munch was a Norwegian painter. His best known work
column4: The Scream
column5: has become one of the iconic images of world art. His childhood was overshadowed by illness
column6: bereavement and the dread of inheriting a mental condition that ran in the family. Studying at the Royal School of Art and Design in Kristiania
column7: Munch began to live a bohemian life under the influence of the nihilist Hans Jæger
column8: who urged him to paint his own emotional and psychological state. From this emerged his distinctive style. Travel brought new influences and outlets. In Paris
column9: he learned much from Paul Gauguin
column10: Vincent van Gogh and Henri de Toulouse-Lautrec
column11: especially their use of colour. In Berlin
column12: he met the Swedish dramatist August Strindberg
column13: whom he painted
column14: as he embarked on his major canon The Frieze of Life
column15: depicting a series of deeply-felt themes such as love
column16: anxiety
column17: jealousy and betrayal
column18: steeped in atmosphere. The Scream was conceived in Kristiania. According to Munch
column19: he was out walking at sunset
column20: when he 'heard the enormous
column21: infinite scream of nature'. The painting's agonised face is widely identified with the angst of the modern person. Home Discover Play Nearby Favorites The Lab Sign in Loading… Tartan Tartan is a patterned cloth consisting of criss-crossed
column2: horizontal and vertical bands in multiple colours. Tartans originated in woven wool
column3: but now they are made in many other materials. Scottish tartans usually represent a clan whilst Irish tartans usually represent the county or region where a clan originated. Tartan is made with alternating bands of coloured threads woven as both warp and weft at right angles to each other. The weft is woven in a simple twill
column4: two over—two under the warp
column5: advancing one thread at each pass. This forms visible diagonal lines where different colours cross
column6: which give the appearance of new colours blended from the original ones. The resulting blocks of colour repeat vertically and horizontally in a distinctive pattern of squares and lines known as a sett. Tartan is often called "plaid"
column7: but in Scotland
column8: a plaid is a large piece of tartan cloth
column9: worn as a type of kilt or large shawl. The term plaid is also used in Scotland for an ordinary blanket such as one would have on a bed. The Dress Act of 1746 attempted to bring the warrior clans under government control by banning the tartan and other aspects of Gaelic culture. column6: Belgium Bruegel painted this picture when he was still living in Antwerp and supplying drawings to the engraver Hieronymus Cock. Turning his back on the then-dominant Italian models
column7: he plunges into the then old-fashioned tradition of Hieronymus Bosch’s world. An apparently inextricable mixture of persons and shapes offers itself to our bewildered gaze. Emerging from distant depths in a halo of light
column8: monsters are thrown to earth as from a breaking wave. Angels combat them
column9: led by St Michael
column10: thin as a rake in his golden armour
column11: striking with his sword at the dragon with the seven crowned heads on which he has his foothold. The combat of the archangel with the fallen angels is described in the Book of Revelation (12
column12: 3-9) and was frequently illustrated from the Middle Ages onwards. In Bruegel’s rendering
column13: the violence is expressed not in the bitter nature of the battle – indeed St Michael and his sparse troops do not appear particularly threatened by the demons – but by the intensity of the fall – infernal and endless – of this crawling
column14: hideous multitude that invades the entire surface of the picture
column15: in a remarkable unity of action which increases its impact. By borrowing minutiously observed elements from the plant
column16: animal
column17: mineral and human worlds and combining them to form hybrid
column18: deformed beings
column19: Bruegel invents creatures that are the most repulsive
column20: but also the most curious and fantastic imaginable. Mussel shells grafted onto a gigantic shrimp
column21: a human head with butterfly wings attached to a shapeless
column22: bloated body
column23: a puffy gnome carrying a sundial and with a plumed helmet on his head
column24: viscous fish with arms
column25: lizard scales
column26: crustacean paws… a seemingly endless list. Within the mêlée
column27: every element is differentiated by the scrupulous rendering of the textures. With their long
column28: refined silhouettes
column29: St Michael’s allies
column30: elegantly garbed in delicate
column31: luminously coloured albs
column32: are automatically on the side of the Good
column33: in a state of grace that enables them to dominate effortlessly the monstrous hordes
column34: moving around in a clear and azure sky which is in profound contrast with the darkness reserved for the rebels. Bruegel reveals himself here to be a marvelous colourist
column35: dexterously distributing accents of red
column36: green
column37: blue and white and alternating the dark browns and lighter beige ochres with brio. Text: Véronique Bücken

column4: the first Triceratops ever put on display Smithsonian National Museum of Natural History Washington
column5: DC
column6: United States This Triceratops specimen is named after John Bell Hatcher
column7: the paleontologist who discovered the species in 1888. In 1905
column8: the specimen went on display at the Smithsonian National Museum of Natural History
column9: and for more than 20 years
column10: it was the only example of a Triceratops exhibited anywhere on the planet. Monster mashup But back in 1905
column11: no complete Triceratops skeletons had ever been unearthed. To create the exhibit
column12: paleontologists pieced together bones from 10 different individuals. This created something of a crude composite - Hatcher’s skull was too small
column13: his front legs were different lengths
column14: and his rear feet belonged to an entirely different species - with the wrong number of toes. Hatcher’s posture was also rather ungainly. To match the turn-of-the-century notion that he was a swamp dweller
column15: the specimen’s front end was slung low and crocodile-like
column16: with his elbows nearly at shoulder level. The specimen was the centerpiece of what was then called the “Hall of Extinct Monsters.” He was posed without any suggestion of motion
column17: like a pinned butterfly. Unseen science At the time
column18: dinosaurs were seen as curiosities - sluggish evolutionary first drafts doomed by their own strangeness. “The way they were presented didn’t so much lend itself to opening up a window to science more broadly
column19: ” says Matthew Carrano
column20: Smithsonian’s Curator of Dinosauria . “It was more like
column21: ‘look at these weird objects from the past.’” The preparators of the day treated Hatcher’s bones more like building materials than priceless artifacts. He was locked into his uninspired pose by metal rods and screws drilled directly into his skeleton. “The 1905 mount did irreparable damage to the fossil
column22: ” says Pete Kroehler
column23: a fossil preparator who worked extensively on Hatcher in 1998. But Hatcher was a star in his day
column24: and drew crowds to the museum. Falling fossils Then
column26: a visitor to the museum was admiring Hatcher when a chunk of fossilized pelvis bone fell to the ground
column27: to the dismay of a nearby security guard. A closer look revealed that humidity was causing minerals to grow in the fossilized bones
column28: causing Hatcher to break up from the inside. In 1998
column29: Hatcher was removed from display so conservators could treat the advancing condition
column30: and set about creating a new
column31: more scientifically accurate mount. Hatcher 2.0 The Smithsonian took advantage of Hatcher’s time in conservation to complete the first 3D scan of an entire dinosaur skeleton. This allowed them to adjust Hatcher’s oddly proportioned bones
column32: and to create a 1:6 scale model of the skeleton. With the 3D scan and new physical model that could be easily manipulated
column33: the Smithsonian hosted a symposium of the world’s top Triceratops experts. The group agreed on a more upright posture for Hatcher that remains the scientific community’s best guess at how the dinosaur might have carried itself. The specimen went back on display
column34: posed with his head lowered and one leg raised to suggest he was turning to defend himself. Second death In 2019 the exhibit was reconfigured to show Hatcher lying dead
column35: being eaten by a Tyrannosaurus rex - helping to highlight an extinct ecosystem
column36: with the T. rex at the top as predator
column37: and Triceratops being preyed upon. Carrano said that it's quite possible a T. rex really did scavenge Hatcher after something else had already put an end to the Triceratops. Hatcher’s new display also echoes what brought his remains to the museum in the first place. “For an animal to become a fossil
column38: the animal has to die and it has to become deeply buried
column39: ” says Kirk Johnson
column40: paleontologist and Sant Director of the Smithsonian’s National Museum of Natural History. “So
column41: part of the story Hatcher's new exhibit tells is that he’s on his way to becoming a fossil.” Details Title: Hatcher

مضمّنة في Google Workspace ومصمَّمة للتعاون في المؤسسات. تشمل المزايا الرئيسية إمكانات محسّنة للذكاء الاصطناعي مع Gemini لتعزيز الإنتاجية، وتكاملاً تامًا مع تطبيقات Google Workspace (Gmail وDrive و"تقويم Google")، و"مساحات" مخصّصة للمشاريع الجماعية. يوفّر هذا الإصدار حلاً جيدًا وغير مُلكف من خلال دمج أدوات التواصل، كما يقدّم ميزات أمان قوية مصمّمة للمؤسسات. نعم، Google Chat هو بديل قوي لـ Slack وMicrosoft Teams. يوفّر التطبيق جميع الميزات الأساسية التي تتوقّعها، مثل المراسلة المباشرة والمحادثات الجماعية (المساحات) ومشاركة الملفات. تكمن المزايا الأساسية في تكامله السلس مع منظومة Google Workspace وميزاته القوية المضمَّنة التي تستخدم ذكاء Gemini الاصطناعي، والقادرة على تلخيص المحادثات وتحديد بنود العمل. مع أنّ المنصات الثلاث تقدّم ميزات تواصل أساسية، يتميّز Google Chat بتكامله المباشر مع Google Workspace وإمكاناته المتطوّرة المستندة إلى الذكاء الاصطناعي. "المساحات" في Chat تشبه "القنوات" في Slack وTeams، ولكنها توفّر سهولة أكبر في العثور على المحتوى وتكامل مباشر مع "مجموعات Google". يوفّر "Gemini في Chat" تحسينات فريدة على الإنتاجية لا تتوفّر في الإصدارات العادية من المنتجات المنافسة. توفّر Google عملية منظَّمة للتبديل إلى Google Chat. إذا كان لديك مؤسسة صغيرة، يمكنك استخدام أدوات تصدير البيانات واستيرادها لنقل المحادثات والملفات. أمّا عند نقل البيانات الأكبر حجمًا أو الأكثر تعقيدًا، توفّر Google شركاء نقل بيانات متمرّسين يمكنهم تقديم دعم شامل ومتكامل لضمان الانتقال بسلاسة وبدون فقدان البيانات. نعم، Google Chat هو تطبيق أساسي مشمول بدون تكلفة إضافية في معظم خطط اشتراك Google Workspace. إذا كنت تستخدم Google Workspace حاليًا، يمكنك تفعيل Google Chat بسهولة من خلال "وحدة تحكّم المشرف" لبدء استخدامه. إنّ Gemini، نموذج الذكاء الاصطناعي من Google والمدمج في Chat، يعزّز الإنتاجية بشكل كبير من خلال تلخيص المحادثات الطويلة واستخراج بنود العمل تلقائيًا ومساعدتك في العثور على إجابات من مناقشات فريقك. ويساعدك أيضًا في الكتابة من خلال ميزات مثل "الكتابة الذكية" و"الردود السريعة"، ما يتيح لفريقك التواصل بكفاءة أكبر، بالإضافة إلى ترجمة اللغات تلقائيًا لدعم الفِرق العالمية أو المتعدّدة الثقافات. تم تصميم Google Chat بميزات أمان مصمّمة للمؤسسات. وهو يتضمّن ميزات، مثل منع فقدان البيانات (DLP) والتشفير التام بين الأطراف والتكامل مع Google Vault للاحتفاظ بالبيانات وجمع الأدلة الإلكترونية. يتوافق Chat مع اللوائح التنظيمية الرئيسية في المجال وقوانين خصوصية البيانات، بما في ذلك HIPAA وGDPR، ما يضمن حماية بيانات مؤسستك. يتكامل Google Chat بشكل كبير مع Google Workspace لتوفير سير عمل سلس. يمكنك بدء محادثة مباشرةً من صندوق البريد الوارد في Gmail، وجدولة الاجتماعات في "تقويم Google" بدون مغادرة المحادثة، والتعاون فورًا في العمل على "مستندات Google" و"جداول بيانات Google" و"العروض التقديمية من Google" ضمن مساحة في Chat. وهذا يغنيك عن الحاجة إلى التبديل باستمرار بين التطبيقات. نعم، يتيح Google Chat استخدام مجموعة واسعة من التطبيقات التابعة لجهات خارجية. يمكنك العثور على التطبيقات وإضافتها من Google Workspace Marketplace Comms & Meetings ▾ Gmail Google Chat Google Calendar Google Tasks Google Groups Google Meet Google Meet hardware Google Voice Content & Collaboration ▾ Google Drive Google Docs Google Sheets Google Slides Google Forms Google Keep Google Sites Google Vids Gemini ▾ Gemini Gemini App Gemini Notebook Workspace Studio Admin & Security ▾ Admin console Security and Compliance Directory Sync Google Workspace Migrate Google Vault Identity MDM SSO Education ▾ Google Workspace for Education Google Classroom More ▾ Google Workspace Marketplace API Google Apps Script AppSheet Mobile iOS Android Beta Additional Google services Weekly Recap Other Google Workspace Add-ons rss_feed arrow_back Back September 1, 2023 Evolving collaboration in Google Chat with smart chips Google Chat Next 2023 Rapid Release This announcement is part of Google Cloud Next ‘23 . Visit the Workspace Blog to learn more about the new Google Chat. What’s changing In 2021, we launched smart canvas to drive the next era of collaboration in Google Workspace. Since then, we’ve added numerous smart chips to Google Docs and Sheets that enable you to preview and access rich, context-setting information and files within your documents and spreadsheets. Today, we’re excited to announce smart chips in Google Chat on web. When composing a message in Chat, typing “@” will now display a list of suggestions for files to include as smart chips. You can search files by typing the name of the file, and the results will be based on files you’ve used most recently. Once a file is selected, you can insert it directly into your message. Who’s impacted End users Why you’d use it Many people take a number of collaborative actions in Chat so they can get work done faster. For example, you may share project files in a direct message or space to gather quick feedback from stakeholders. This feature reduces friction for senders by eliminating the need to separately find files within Drive and then copy/paste them into a Chat message. Now, users can send files as smart chips so they are compact and readable in a message, without leaving Chat. Additional details An in-line preview of the file chip will be shown while composing the message, similar to when pasting the URL of the file into Chat. This can be removed by clicking on the dismiss button before sending the message or at any point when editing the message. Getting started Admins: There is no admin control for this feature. End users: In Google Chat on web, type “@” followed by a file name to search for a file and insert it directly into a message. Visit the Help Center to learn more about sending & sharing files in Google Chat . Note: Mobile users can receive and click on smart chips, but cannot insert them on the Chat mobile app at this time. حماية بياناتك وبقاؤك خاضعًا للتغطية يمكنك التحكُّم في جميع العناصر. ويمكنك ضبط عمليات وقواعد الاحتفاظ بالبيانات من تطبيقات معينة Google Workspace لنطاق كامل أو وحدات تنظيمية مُحدّدة. العثور عمَّا تبحث عنه الآن وتصديره في أي وقت يمكنك استرداد المعلومات القيّمة، حتى من الحسابات المُعلَّقة. ويُعد ذلك وسيلة ذكية لجمع ما يحتاجه الفريق القانوني ومنع فقدان البيانات مع تغيير الموظفين. التأكُّد من الحفاظ على التفاصيل المهمة بأمان يمكنك مَنحُ فريقك القانوني ما يحتاج إليه للبقاء جاهزًا. وتسمح لك أداة Vault بالاحتفاظ ببيانات المستخدمين من تطبيقات محدّدة Google Workspace من خلال عمليات الاحتفاظ بالبيانات. التصدير إلى التنسيقات القياسية بسهولة يمكن تصدير جميع أنواع المحتوى التي تم استردادها من خلال البحث إلى التنسيقات القياسية للمراجعة الإضافية، بما في ذلك نتائج أي حساب مُرخّص. تقارير تدقيق تُتيح لك تتبُّع النشاط يمكنك تتبع نشاط المستخدمين داخل Vault، إذ تتيح لك مسارات التدقيق القوية الاطلاع على عمليات البحث ومرات مشاهدة المحتوى وعمليات التصدير والمزيد. الأسئلة الشائعة يُرجى الاطّلاع على الأسئلة الشائعة لمزيد من المعلومات. توسيع الكل الاكتشاف الإلكتروني أو جمع الأدلة الإلكترونية، هو عملية السعي والبحث عن معلومات متوفرة بتنسيق إلكتروني. ويتم إجراؤها في إطار الاستجابة للمسائل القانونية والتحقيقات. في حال حذف مستخدم، ستتم إزالة جميع البيانات المرتبطة بحساب هذا المستخدم من Google. وفي إطار أفضل الممارسات، توصي Google بتعليق حسابات المستخدمين بدلاً من حذفها. يتم تضمين أداة Vault مع إصدارات Google Workspace للشركات والمؤسسات بدون فرض أي تكلفة إضافية عليك. الإعداد سهل للغاية، لِنبدأ اليوم إذا احتجت إلى المساعدة، يمكنك التواصل مع فريق الدعم عبر البريد الإلكتروني، والمحادثة، والهاتف على مدار الساعة وطوال أيام الأسبوع. column52: Not Impressed with Functionality 10/04/2019 kiera113 I was hoping this would bridge the gap between my WearOS powered fossil smartwatch and Apple Health so I could get more use out of the health data and the Google Fit functionality of the watch. Unfortunately no such features. The app has read only permissions with Apple Health so it only organizes data from that app into Google’s. It does not link with WearOS so data from the smartwatch does not go directly to Google Fit’s app so that is still a problem for me. I like that it puts the focus on heart health in a “weight watchers” kinda way— points instead of steps or calories to get a bigger picture view of how to improve overall health. But I’m not getting my progress counted from my smartwatch anyways. Overall

الاصطناعي، ما يوفّر للشركات حلاً مرنًا وآمنًا وقابلاً للتوسع. تجربة Meet للعمل تسجيل الدخول اجتماعات على مستوى النشاط التجاري باستخدام Google Workspace توفّر لك حزمة Google Workspace التطبيقات التي تحبها، مثل Google Meet، مع ميزات مدفوعة للأنشطة التجارية. اجتماعات فيديو مستندة إلى الذكاء الاصطناعي (AI) بإمكان "Gemini في Meet" تسجيل الملاحظات وترجمة المحادثات في الوقت الفعلي وتحسين جودة الفيديو/الصوت الضعيفة، لتمكينك من التركيز على المحادثة الجارية. مزيد من المعلومات المشاركة الكاملة في الاجتماعات المختلطة يمكنك التعاون بسهولة مع الفِرق على اختلاف أحجامها، من أي جهاز، سواء من المنزل أو المكتب أو أي مكان آخر. مزيد من المعلومات الأمان وحماية البيانات يمكنك إجراء اجتماعات آمنة من خلال عناصر تحكُّم متقدّمة خاصة بالمضيف، وتدابير لمنع إساءة الاستخدام وتشفير تلقائي. مزيد من المعلومات سهولة الإدارة والتوافق مع المؤسسات من خلال الانتقال إلى Meet لإجراء اجتماعات الفيديو على مستوى المؤسسة، يمكنك توفير تكاليف الاشتراك والحصول على ميزات الإدارة السلِسة في "وحدة تحكُّم مشرف Google Workspace". مزيد من المعلومات تستخدمها المؤسسات العالمية والأنشطة التجارية المحلية منصة فعالة وقابلة للتعديل ومحسنة لتلائم التطبيقات وعمليات الدمج التعاون واستخدام لوح المعلومات مع الفِرق في Google Meet يمكنك تحسين التعاون من خلال دمج الأدوات التابعة لجهات خارجية في اجتماعك، مثل تطبيقات لوح المعلومات من Figma وLucidSpark وMiro وغيرها. عرض تطبيقات Meet دمج التطبيقات ومهام سير العمل مع واجهات برمجة التطبيقات وحزم تطوير البرامج (SDK) في Google Meet يمكنك إنشاء التطبيقات وإجراء عمليات الدمج لتتيح للمستخدمين التواصل عبر واجهات برمجة التطبيقات في Google Meet وحزمة Embed SDK وحزمة Add-ons SDK، ما يساهم في تحسين التفاعل. مزيد من المعلومات من روّاد التعاون في مجال عقد اجتماعات الفيديو تم تصنيف Google Workspace كخدمة رائدة في Forrester Wave™‎: الاتصالات الموحدة كخدمة (UCaaS). **"ويل ماكيون وايت"،**محلل بيانات أول، Forrester Research الاطّلاع على التقرير نظرًا لسهولة استخدام Google Chat وGoogle Meet وإمكانية طرحهما بسرعة كبيرة، اعتمد موظفو Kärcher في جميع أنحاء العالم قنوات الاتصال الإبداعية والشخصية ترجمات لكسر حواجز اللغة قريبًا: ستساعد ميزة "تدوين الملاحظات نيابةً عني" في تسجيل ملاحظات الاجتماع نعم، يضمّ Google Meet ميزات للأمان وحماية الخصوصية على مستوى المؤسسة ، ويشمل تشفير موثوقة مستندة إلى السحابة الإلكترونية وبتصميم آمن من Google، ويتّبع التطبيق إجراءات صارمة في ما يتعلق بمنع الحوادث ورصدها والاستجابة لها للمساعدة في الحفاظ على أمان المستخدمين والبيانات. يتكامل Google What is the pollen index Google's pollen model provides an effective and simple pollen index to help you determine the likelihood of experiencing allergy symptoms from upcoming pollen exposure. This index considers both concentration of allergenic pollen in the air and the likelihood of developing symptoms due to the specific types of pollen present. click the down arrow . Review which members take up space. Members of a family group can only free up space from their own storage usage. You can't affect the storage usage of other family members. Ask the people who use too much space if they can free up Google storage space . Tip: If you want to make changes to your family plan members, learn how to manage your Google family. Learn more about family sharing with Google One The person who shares their storage is called the Google One plan manager. This person can start or stop sharing their Google One family plan at any time. You can share Google One with up to 5 family members. Based on how much storage your family group uses, you can change, upgrade, or downgrade your Google One plan . There are 2 kinds of storage space: personal storage space and shared storage space. Important: The Workspace Individual subscriber’s cloud storage can’t be shared among family members. Each member of the family group gets up to 15 GB of personal storage space for their files: A family member’s files fill up their personal space first . There's also shared storage split between everyone in your family group: After a family member's personal storage gets filled up, their files count toward the shared storage space. Family members can use as much of this available storage as they want. Others in your family won’t have access to your files unless you share them directly. When you make a family group, extra benefits are shown to everyone in your family, except accounts managed by parents . Some benefits go to the first family member who claims them. Learn how family sharing works How family sharing works with Google One For this same video with audio descriptions: How family sharing works with Google One . Requirements for joining a family To join a family group, you need to: Have a Google Account. You can't join a family with a Google Account from your work, school, or other organization. Live in the same country as the family manager. Be part of just one family group. Be in no other family group in the past 12 months. What happens when you stop sharing Google One family plan members will: Stop using your available storage. If they run out of storage, their files will stay safe, but they won't be able to store anything new. Learn more about what happens when they run out of space . Lose access to experts who answer questions about Google products. Lose the ability to find or claim benefits. Many of the same effects can happen if the Google One plan manager decides to leave the family group , or if they delete or remove someone from the family group . Share AI credits with your family You can share AI credits with your Google One family group. However, only the plan manager can buy additional AI credits, upgrade, or downgrade memberships. Learn how to manage your AI credits with Google One . Get help with family storage Find your family’s storage usage If you’re the Google One plan manager and can’t find how much your storage is used, follow the steps above to make sure family sharing is on. Information shared with family members When you join a family, your family members can find your name, photo, and email address. They can also find how much shared storage each family member uses. Family members aren’t able to find your photos, videos, or other items unless you directly share them. Family members didn't get invite to join the family group Learn how to join a family . If they still don't get an invite, ask a Google expert for help . Transfer available storage to another account The Family Manager shares their storage with up to 5 accounts, but only one member of the group can be Family Manager. Use individual & family storage If you have a Google One Membership, you can enjoy both your individual storage and the Family Plan Manager’s shared storage. However, you have to use your individual storage up before you use the shared storage. What happens to your storage when you join a family If you already have a Google One Membership when your family adds you to their plan, you can use both memberships and storage. However, you can’t upgrade or downgrade your individual membership. Once you use up your individual account’s storage, you can start to use the family’s storage. Tap Privacy & Settings . Under “Your Data,” tap Delete profile & game data . Under “Delete individual game data,” find the game data you want to remove. Tap Delete . Delete your Play Games profile and all Play Games data If you delete your Play Games profile, all of your Play Games information will be deleted from your Google Account, your gamer name will become available to other users, your followers, anyone you follow, and gaming stats associated with your profile will be deleted. Depending on how developers built the games you've downloaded, deleting your Play Games profile may also delete your in-game achievements or progress, experience points and scores on leaderboards. To learn more about managing your in-game achievements or progress, you can contact the game developer . If you delete your Play Games profile, you may also not be able to access certain services if they require an active Play Games profile, such as Google Play Games on PC. Important: Your Play Games profile collects your gaming activity. That activity is separate from Play History data. Deleting your Play Games profile or specific data from your Play Games profile will not delete data from your Play History. The reverse is also true. Here’s how to control both: Google Play Games data : You can delete data for specific games or permanently delete your entire Play Games profile. You can do this in your Play Games profile settings. If you delete data here, it removes it from your Play Games profile. It doesn’t delete it from your Google Account's Play History. Play History data: If you have Play History turned on in your Google Account, and the option to include app usage data is turned on, Play will continue to save information about when you play a game and for how long. You can find or delete your Play History at any time in Personalization in Play . When you delete Play History, Google still retains some data. For example, Play keeps information about the items you’ve purchased and downloaded so you’ll still have access to them. Deleting your Play History doesn’t affect information collected by other settings or features you’ve turned on. For example, if you’ve created a Play Games Profile, it’ll keep information about your app activity to show your game stats. Deleting your Play History also doesn’t affect data that has been disconnected from your account which Google retains to provide, understand, improve, and develop our services. column252: and add Irish Gaelic pronunciation!! Mar 20 Kevin James Wright I think the handwriting search for Japanese translation in Google Translate is second-to-none
column253: because it uses shape recognition incredibly well. But the sound pronunciations of the Japanese characters almost always differ from their transliteration into Latin alphabet below the text! Kanji are characters that typically have at least 2 different pronunciations depending on how they are used. This is not something you can trust an artificial intelligence to properly program or be able to discern!!From a language-learner’s perspective
column254: Google Translate cannot reliably be used or trusted. It is designed for those who don’t care about learning other languages. This pragmatic approach has its benefits
column255: because it can translate semantically even when there is a mistake in the language being translated. But this also leads to deficits in the app’s ability to assist in learning. The discrepancy between the audio pronunciation and the transliteration of Japanese characters is especially bad. column263: then use the Benkyō app for Apple devices. One of the top 2 translator apps 10/21/2018 YsniperY I’ve been using this app from the start and the updates have all been great. My review can only be said for the English/German translation. I don’t know how accurate it is for other languages. The best update so far as usability was the delay from when the user stops speaking and the time the app stops listening in order to translate. When learning a new language the speaker is obviously going to have pauses in order to think for a second. The app used to assume that was all the speaker intended and then would translate. Horribly irritating. I (and probably others) made a suggestion to the team and they updated it. Now a pause won’t automatically end until more time goes by. I wish there was a setting or button that the user could use to modify/set the duration of a pause before auto-translating for a better learning/teaching experience but for now the update has been a God send. Also the update a while back on translating written words from a book etc is simply incredible. I love it. I totally thought it was magic. I have found that some words or sentences aren’t translated perfectly but that’s probably more to the app not knowing the whole story or context of what the speaker is trying to convey but it does a pretty good job. I find using capital letters at the start of a sentence and good punctuation critical when you type your sentence in order to improve the translation. The list of synonyms for a word is very helpful as well. I’ve been using the Pimsleur language courses (CDs) for years and it’s uncanny how accurate the app is with those. I was also told my German is quite good by native speakers when I was in Switzerland and I truly feel that this app was a part of my overall learning experience. column29: environments and behaviors — even if the unfamiliar bird actually belongs to an entirely separate family. That’s why there are more searches for general bird terms

column50: it doesn’t require much of anything. There’s a brand of birding that fosters a gentle approach of simply noticing and observing birds for nothing other than the joy of doing so — no deeper knowledge or superzoom cameras required. Over the last decade
column51: birding has become a more inclusive activity
column52: with organizations popping up around the country to cater to people of all backgrounds and abilities. The mission of these groups is to cultivate communities of birders who don’t necessarily identify with the hard-core

column54: there’s a good chance you’ll see one that changes everything. Part Two The Spark Bird It might seem challenging to get from “duck” to the more specific Green-winged Teal . But the identification process starts with a simple step: caring to know a bird’s name in the first place. Often
column55: this happens after a particular encounter with a very special bird — a so-called “spark bird.” A spark bird is the catalyst to wanting to discover more. Every spark bird is personal because people are moved by birds for different reasons. Sometimes it’s the flash of color or striking patterns of the feathers. Other times it’s a mesmerizing behavior or an unexpectedly close encounter. But whatever the case
column56: a spark bird becomes the gateway to identifying other birds. column73: Google search data shows that only 98 bird species have significant search interest across the U.S. An additional 11 birds have search interest in at least one state. Birds with measurable Google search interest Solid | Popular across the US Striped | Popular in at least one state The colorful areas of the egg spotlight the birds that pique our interest. For instance
column74: we frequently Google species of hawks
column75: owls and other raptors. We also can’t get enough of the woodpeckers. It figures that we
column76: collectively
column77: are curious about these birds given their fascinating abilities and behaviors. Grouping birds
column78: either by shape or family
column79: is both an art and a science. Whether a species belongs with one group versus another can be a matter of debate. We also often search for species of game birds and ducks
column80: particularly the hunting breeds like the Northern Pintail and the Wood Duck . We love Northern Cardinals and Blue Jays
column81: with their eye-catching shades of reds and blues. And we gravitate to the elegant silhouettes of Great Egrets and Great Blue Herons . On the other hand
column82: it seems we don’t tend to search for species of gulls
column83: terns and seabirds. Perhaps this is because more than half of the U.S. population doesn’t live near a shore. Furthermore
column84: seabirds can be tricky to distinguish
column85: so we are less likely to search for their species names and instead fall back on general labels like seagull . The same case could be made for the myriad of little brown birds like sparrows
column86: warblers and chickadees. Part Three Find a Bird
column87: Share a Bird The more effort you put into researching a bird’s name
column88: the more satisfaction when you finally identify it. But the digital age is all about instant gratification. Social media allows us to share photos of birds and tap into online communities for identification help. A growing number of apps including Merlin Bird ID (created by the Cornell Lab of Ornithology)
column89: Seek (by iNaturalist) and Birda use photo identification technology and artificial intelligence to instantly suggest possible bird species based on photos
column90: even if they’re blurry. Merlin takes things a step further
column91: offering possible identifications based on birdsong recordings. Oftentimes
column92: though
column93: we don’t have our phones at the ready
column94: especially during spontaneous bird encounters. In those cases
column95: we need to rely on our memory of a bird in order to identify it. Reaching out to the birder community (in person or on digital forums) can help narrow the search. So
column96: too
column97: can chatbots
column98: like this one from Google’s Gemini: "Spark Bird" AI Assistant Hello! I'm your AI bird expert. I can help you in two ways: Identify a bird: I can try to figure out what U.S. bird you saw. Please describe what you remember about the bird: its colors
column99: its rough size
column100: where you saw it and any other details you can remember. “There was a bright red bird with black around the beak and eyes at my bird feeder.” “I saw a large bird with a white head and tail soaring over a lake in Washington.” “I spotted a dark bird with pink wings and underbelly on a rocky cliff in the Colorado mountains.” Learn about a bird: Ask me about a specific U.S. bird to get more information
column101: such as breeding season
column102: population
column103: Google Trend ranking and more. “I want to know more about the Cedar Waxwing” “Tell me about the Burrowing Owl” AI can make mistakes. Please verify important information. Digital tools don’t just benefit us; they also benefit the birds. The public eBird database
column104: run by the Cornell Lab of Ornithology
column105: has been recognized as the largest citizen science birdwatching project in the world
column106: surpassing 2 billion bird observations in 2025. When you enter your bird sighting into the eBird app
column107: you contribute to an enormous repository of information about population trends
column108: migration patterns and habitat use. All of this information can help scientists identify threats to the birds and shape conservation policy. Part Four What We See — and What We Don’t Snowy Owls are rare. The estimated 15
column109: 000 that exist in North America stick mainly to Alaska and Canada
column110: where they breed
column111: and don’t often visit the lower 48 states. On the rarest of occasions
column112: one may end up in Central Park. Snowy Owls are the 465th most observed species on eBird and they rank 554th for total North American population
column113: according to Partners in Flight
column114: which maintains an Avian Conservation Assessment database . That puts Snowy Owls toward the bottom of the list of North American birds. But
column115: despite their obscurity
column116: Snowy Owl is the 20th most Googled bird species in the U.S. Other elusive birds
column117: particularly owls like the Great Horned Owl and the American Barn Owl
column118: also make the top 20. The chart below lists the 21 most searched birds in the U.S. (middle column) compared with eBird observations (left) and U.S. and Canada populations (right). Species with significant search interest have a colored bar. These are the same birds that were highlighted in the egg
column119: above. (A solid color bar means the species is in Google’s top 21
column120: and a hatched bar means it ranks lower down.) Chart: Search Interest vs. Real World Data A bar chart comparing three rankings of the top 21 birds: eBird Observations (what people see/report)
column121: Google Search Interest (what people search)
column122: and Population (how many exist). There is a strong correlation between sightings and searches; birds we attribute to seeing often are also searched often. However
column123: there is a disconnect with population size; many abundant but small or elusive birds (like sparrows) are rarely searched
column124: while rarer but iconic birds (like Eagles and Owls) are searched frequently. Looking at the lines connecting the three lists
column125: it’s apparent that what we spot in the wild is also what we tend to search for on Google: About half of the species on the eBird observation list (on the left) are also on the Google search list (in the middle). Only the American Crow
column127: doesn’t register on Google Trends. This is likely because most people search simply for crow instead of its species name. At the same time
column128: only four birds on the most populous list (along the right) are also on the most searched list. This is in part because many small bird species like the Blue-gray Gnatcatcher and the Savannah Sparrow are abundant but well hidden in their protected habitats
column129: away from our eyes — and our curious minds. In fact
column130: out of the five most populous birds in North America
column131: three of them do not even register on Google Trends. (And we’re talking about hundreds of millions of these little feathery balls flying across the skies!) Although we Google some rare and elusive birds like the owls
column132: the rarest of the birds fail to spark our curiosity. Over 200 species
column133: accounting for nearly a third of U.S. birds
column134: need urgent conservation
column135: according to a 2025 report published by the North American Bird Conservation Initiative
column136: and 112 of them have lost more than 50% of their populations in the past 50 years. We don’t Google them because they exist on the fringes of our world
column137: even though it’s these birds that most need our attention. Part Five Species We Know and Love The Bald Eagle is one species that got our attention just in the nick of time. In the mid 1900s the species was nearly wiped out by habitat destruction and DDT insecticide poisoning. The species had a few things working in its favor: It is the emblem of the U.S. and it has also been meaningfully symbolic to people throughout history — from centuries of Indigenous peoples to the Founding Fathers to contemporary Americans. Through publicity and conservation efforts
column138: Bald Eagles became an icon of the environmental movement. Today Bald Eagle is the top searched bird nationally and also in 26 U.S. states. (In the remaining states
column139: it places second or third
column140: except for Hawaii
column141: the only state where it doesn’t live in the wild.) Another bird species that many Americans know and love is the Northern Cardinal. Northern Cardinal is the second most searched species in the U.S. and the top searched species in 16 states. Its popularity no doubt stems from the males’ bright red plumage and its frequent appearances in gardens and feeders. It ranks highly in just about every state east of the Rockies
column142: but doesn’t crack the top 10 in the western states that are outside its habitat range. Some species
column143: such as the Blue Jay and American Robin are highly searched in many states — which is why they are
column144: respectively
column145: the third and fourth ranked birds nationally — but neither has the top spot in any state. The map below shows the most searched bird by state. Hover over Select a state to see its top 10 species on Google Trends. Map: Most Searched Bird by State A hexagon tile map of the US showing the top searched bird in each state. The Bald Eagle is the most popular
column146: claiming the top spot in 26 states. The Northern Cardinal follows
column147: leading mostly in the East. Bald Eagle Northern Cardinal Cooper’s Hawk Sandhill Crane Barred Owl Hawaiian Goose State-level rankings give a glimpse into what draws humans to search different birds. In Nebraska
column149: Sandhill Crane is the most searched
column150: likely because the North Platte River valley hosts the largest gathering in the world
column151: with up to 600
column152: 000 cranes stopping to rest and feed for about six weeks before migrating north. [*] In Louisiana and Mississippi
column153: Mallard and Wood Duck are in the top five most searched
column154: likely because duck hunting is such a popular pastime in those states’ extensive marshlands. Cooper’s Hawk
column155: on the other hand
column156: is a search term that ranks highly in a few states that also happen to have a restaurant chain of the same name
column157: suggesting that Google Trends is unable to distinguish between the bird and the establishment. Part Six Paying Attention Long before social media feeds and birding apps
column158: birders relied on analog systems to get information. Rare bird hotlines — phone numbers run by local Audubon chapters or birding clubs — catered to enthusiasts hungry for news of a vagrant warbler or storm-swept gannet. Callers would dial in
column159: listen to a recorded message
column160: and
column161: if they were lucky
column162: hear that an awesome bird had touched down nearby. Today
column163: news of a rare sighting travels very differently. An alert on a WhatsApp group or social media or eBird can ignite a frenzy within minutes
column164: drawing crowds to parks and street corners with binoculars in hand. Which is exactly what happened when the Snowy Owl appeared in New York City. Word traveled fast and people who had never used a field guide suddenly wanted to know everything about this arctic wanderer. Rare bird alerts such as this routinely produce Google search spikes resulting from the rush of discovery. Beyond these sudden (and often localized) bursts of search activity
column165: Googling birds follows a seasonal rhythm
column166: as shown in the below chart of the last 10 years. [ In case not all the years between 2016 - 2025 are visible
column167: you can move the line chart left and right to see more years. ] × Chart: Seasonal Search Trends A line chart showing Google search trends for birds over the last 10 years. It reveals a distinct annual pattern with search interest peaking every spring (April/May)
column168: coinciding with migration. There was a notable surge in interest during the pandemic (Spring 2020/2021). Springtime surges Every year there is a pronounced rise in Google searches in April and May
column169: two major spring migration months. This is when millions of birds are on the move
column170: budding trees make sightings easier and birdsong activity peaks. It’s also when the world feels alive again and we venture outside to notice the world around us. Pandemic peak That seasonal pulse was amplified during the pandemic
column171: when search activity for bird terms rose considerably. With travel limited and daily routines stripped back
column172: we paid closer attention to our immediate surroundings and birds became an accessible source of entertainment just outside our windows. A bit out of line The rhythms of bird migration and Googling vary somewhat from species to species. Bald Eagle [ ● ] ticks up a little earlier in the year
column173: in line with peak nesting season in February and March. Searches for Snowy Owl [ ● ]
column174: Snow Goose [ ● ] and other cold weather species peak in the winter months. And searches for Common Raven [ ● ] and Rock Pigeon [ ● ] don’t have much seasonality at all
column175: as these are year-round birds. Whatever month or season it is
column176: birds are everywhere
column177: from the docile Mourning Doves in the grass to the predatory Peregrine Falcons on the cliffsides. Yet we often don’t even notice them
column178: let alone search for them on Google
column179: or on birding apps
column180: or in field guides. Most of the time
column181: they fade into the background of our lives. There are many ways you can bring birds into focus into your own life
column183: for instance
column184: joining a birding community
column186: or cracking open a birding book. But the easiest way is simply to pay attention. Once you do
column187: birds have a way of giving back
column188: instilling you with joy

column17: Google News and YouTube. Find stories and terms people are paying attention to. How Trends works. Google Trends allows you to see the topics people are—or aren’t—following
column18: practically in real time. Journalists can use this information to explore potential story ideas
column19: and can also feature Trends data within news stories to illustrate a general level of interest in
column20: say

column23: Google News
column24: or YouTube. Trending Stories are collected based on Google’s Knowledge Graph technology
column25: which gathers search information from those three Google platforms to detect when stories are trending based on the relative spike in volume and the absolute volume of searches. The Featured insights at the top of the new Google Trends homepage are curated by News Lab to highlight additional data patterns or interesting trends. On the homepage. The Trends homepage indicates what topics are trending right now
column26: which can be helpful when choosing a story to write about. To explore how Google data can be used to tell stories
column27: click one of the examples under Latest Stories and Insights. Exploring your own topics. In addition to what you see on the homepage
column28: you can explore and gauge interest in virtually any topic
column29: which can be useful for developing story ideas. Let’s say you’re doing a story on the U.S. presidential election
column30: and want to compare the election process with that of India’s General elections happening in the same year. Just use the Trends search bar: Step 1 Enter the India General Election in the Google Trends search bar at the top of the homepage. Press Return to see your results. Step 2 Your results page will feature data visualizations for Interest over time and Interest by subregion
column31: as well as lists of Related topics and Related queries. Step 3 You can add topics for simultaneous comparison by clicking + Compare and typing in your search term. Step 4 To remove or edit a topic
column32: hover over its box and click the three dots that appear. Then click Remove. Step 5 You can also search for multiple terms simultaneously just by writing them into the Add a search term box. Comparing groups of terms. You can compare up to five groups of terms at one time and up to 25 terms in each group. Group terms together by using + Add. Explore by language. If you enter a search term using non-Latin characters
column33: you’ll see data from all countries or regions that use those characters. For example
column34: if you enter 選挙

column36: your results will not include much data from the United States. You can easily compare searches of the same term in different languages. Using the election example
column37: just enter search term 選挙 in the first search box
column38: then enter election in the + Compare search box. Narrowing or expanding your search by geography and time. On the results page under the search bar
column39: use the dropdowns Worldwide and 2004-present to refine your exploration further by region and/or time period. More about Trends. Information on how to better understand Google Trends data and read its charts can be found in our Google Trends: Interpreting the Data tutorial
column40: and also in the Trends Help centre accessible from the menu in the upper left of the homepage. Pairing NCI with Google Trends News Consumer Insights (NCI)
column41: our free of cost Google News Initiative data tool
column42: gives you in-depth data about your audience's behavior on your news website. Google Trends shows you the overall popularity of search terms over time. Use them together to: Validate your findings: See if rising engagement with a topic on your site aligns with growing search interest in that topic overall. Identify content opportunities: Discover trending topics that you might not be covering adequately on your site. Refine your content strategy: Tailor your content to match the evolving interests of your audience and the broader public. Essentially
column43: News Consumer Insights (NCI) tells you what's popular on your site
column44: while Google Trends tells you what's popular in the world . column34: we’ve already heard that data on the Trends Explore tool is indexed and normalized. But what does this actually mean? Indexing: Google Trends data is pulled from a random

column31: Troubleshoot SIP Link setup . Bandwidth Estimation for SIP Link SIP Link over the Internet will need to account for the appropriate bandwidth capacity for the Internet connection. SIP Link to User Call (Inbound Call) or User to SIP Link Call (Outbound Call) Each SIP Link call to a user will take 84kbps(SIP Link side using g.711a/mu) + 50kbps (client side using Opus) = 134Kbps. If we have 100 simultaneous calls then the bandwidth required is (134Kbps x 100) = 13400 Kbps or 13.4Mbps. User to User Call (Intra Google Voice call) Each User to User call will take 50kbps (client-A side using Opus) + 50kbps (client side using Opus) = 100Kbps. Similarly
